title: Emperor Claudius Formally Bans Druidism
description: Emperor Claudius issued a formal ban on Druidism around 49 CE, following earlier partial restrictions under Augustus, completing the suppression of this Celtic priestly class in Roman-controlled territories. Roman writers associated Druids with human sacrifice and magical practices, making them targets of imperial religious regulation. The suppression of Druidism represents a significant instance of Roman religious persecution directed at a non-Roman priestly tradition perceived as politically dangerous and magically threatening. This suppression would later influence the Christianization of Celtic regions and the gradual transformation of Druidic lore into folk memory.
historiographical_note: Miranda Green and Ronald Hutton have examined the Roman suppression of Druidism as part of a broader pattern of suppressing non-Roman religious specialists, noting that Roman accounts of Druidic human sacrifice may reflect propaganda rather than reality.
source_method: Published scholarship; Suetonius Claudius 25; Pliny Natural History 30.13
